title: Social Media Influencer Marketing and Consumer Buying Behaviour: The Mediating Roles of Brand Trust and Electronic Word-of-Mouth
content: Influencer marketing on social media has emerged as a significant new communication channel as creators are able to integrate product attributes, storytelling and engagement with their followers. Reach and engagement do not necessarily lead to trust and purchase, however. This study investigates the evidence that explains how influencer marketing affects trust in brand and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM), in relation to consumer purchase behaviour. Specifically, it answers two research questions: What evidence is there to synthesize the impact of creators and influencer-generated content on consumers? What mechanisms have been identified to understand the influence of influencer marketing on purchase intention and its mediators? Two secondary sources were selected for the search, which produced ten articles on the influence of creator attributes and content on consumer responses, ten systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the general influence of influencer marketing, and seven articles on eWOM and trust. The analysis of the synthesis from the meta-analyses shows the complex moderation patterns caused by the differences in moderators such as the message, creator, audience, or platform, where credibility is an important mechanism. The studies on trust and eWOM suggest the importance of credibility, high quality of information and social recommendations, although most results are limited to self-reported research intentions. Overall, eWOM and trust are understood as two interacting mechanisms that influence purchase intention, wherein trust lowers risk perception while eWOM provides high-quality information and social interaction. Recommendations include the use of transparent advertising disclosures, matching product and creator, credible assertions and linking engagement to sales.
